One day you, too, will know that you are God the Father, for you are he who inspired the psalmist to say: “I will tell of the decree of the Lord.” You are that Lord who inspired him to write the words: “Thou art my son, today I have begotten thee.”

quote_original: Let us assume that this is a dream and everything is perfect.
context_before: it is more difficult to control because it appears so real and independent of your perception. But it can be controlled by a simple act of assumption.
context_after: You are happy and content and all is right in your world. Then persuade yourself of the reality of your assumption. quote_original: If you don’t think it is a dream, take some section of your life that seems beyond redemption and rearrange it in your mind’s eye.
context_before: Then the dream you and I are dreaming began.

quote_original: The priests, rabbis, and ministers are looking for his coming, but they will look in vain. Jesus has already come or they couldn’t breathe. He is their life, but they do not know it.
context_before: The Old Testament is an adumbration – a foreshadowing in a not altogether conclusive or immediately evident way. The New is its interpretation and fulfillment. If you hear the word, “Jesus” and think of a man other than yourself, you do not know him.
context_after: One day, however, he will awaken in them as the being in whom he awakens.

rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1969-10-10 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: What I have told you tonight concerning the coming of Christ is the only foundation.
context_before: Try it.
context_after: You will never disprove my words, for I am not speaking from speculation or theory, but from experience. When this little garment I now wear is taken away, I will no longer be a part of this age, for I have awakened from this dream called life. And one day, when your dream is over, the series of events which I have just mapped out for you will unfold within you; and you, too, will awaken and return as the one being who began the venture.
